extracted.intended_audience: monarchs, patrons, university governors, and learned scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Practical recommendations and evaluative standards for promoting, organizing, and preserving learning — aimed at sovereigns, founders, and university governors to improve institutions, books, and scholars and to identify gaps in knowledge. Emphasizes foundations, libraries, salaries, experimental apparatus, curricular order, histories, and the surveying and designation of neglected fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three objects of works toward learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Works and acts of merit towards learning should concern three objects: the places of learning, the books of learning, and the persons of the learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three classes (places, books, persons) are the primary domains in which patrons and governments should act to preserve, propagate, and improve knowledge; each demands distinct kinds of interventions and supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundations for places of learning (fourfold support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works which concern the seats and places of learning are four—foundations and buildings; endowments with revenues; endowments with franchises and privileges; and institutions and ordinances for government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such provisions should aim to secure quietness and privateness of life and to discharge cares and troubles so scholars can pursue study; physical infrastructure, financial stability, legal privileges, and sound governance are all necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support books via libraries and improved editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Works touching books are two—first, libraries as repositories; second, new editions of authors with more correct impressions, faithful translations, profitable glosses, and diligent annotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Libraries preserve the relics of learning 'exempted from the wrong of time', while careful new editions and annotations make texts more usable and reliable for succeeding ages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support persons: designate and reward readers and writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Works pertaining to learned persons are two—the reward and designation of readers in established sciences, and the reward and designation of writers and inquirers for parts of learning not sufficiently laboured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide stable posts and honorific/financial encouragement both to sustain the guardians of existing knowledge and to incentivize inquiry into neglected or new fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction is principal over mere abundance
rubrics_metrics.description: Among ways to promote learning (reward, direction, conjunction of labours), direction (wise election and choice of means) is the principal means of progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-chosen course or mean often achieves more than greater effort without guidance; policy and correct selection of priorities outweigh mere accumulation of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endowments should not be limited to professions; support universal learning
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a defect that foundations are commonly dedicated to professions and none left free to arts and sciences at large; foundations should support philosophy and universality, not only professional training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over-specialization of collegiate endowments hinders progression of sciences and deprives states of broadly educated men fit for public service; encourage root-level, fundamental studies rather than only profession-bound chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate salaries and endowments for public lectures/readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Public lectures and readers are often ill-paid; to have sciences flourish, readers must be endowed sufficiently to attract the ablest men and to permit them to dedicate their lives to teaching and generating sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endowments must be proportionate to what practitioners earn; readers should have equal sustenance with active professionals so they will not be outcompeted and the 'stores of sciences' remain well-guarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide experimental apparatus and cover expenses for investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Many sciences, especially natural philosophy and physic, require instruments (spheres, globes, astrolabes, maps), gardens for simples, dissection facilities, furnaces, engines, and allowances for experiment expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patrons should fund material apparatus and pay for experimenters' expenses (analogous to intelligence bills) so practical, operative study and disclosure of nature can proceed; support for practical contrivances is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance must inspect and reform university usages
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a defect in lack of consultation and visitation by governors and princes; authorities should examine whether readings, exercises, and customs are well instituted and ground amendments where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-examination of ancient customs in light of their original times helps remove weak or ignorant practices; active oversight and willingness to reform university orders is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay teaching logic and rhetoric until students are ripe
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars at universities come too soon and too unripe to logic and rhetoric; these arts are fitter for graduates than novices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching judgment (logic) and ornament (rhetoric) to empty minds lacking material inflows causes degeneration into sophistry and affectation; foundational knowledge should precede these arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises should mix invention and memory to mirror practice
rubrics_metrics.description: University exercises (e.g., speeches) often separate invention and memory too extremely—either fully premeditated or fully extempore—whereas life requires intermixtures of premeditation, invention, notes, and memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame exercises as near as possible to the life of practice to prepare faculties properly; contrived extremes pervert mental motions and fail to prepare for real-world action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster greater mutual intelligence and correspondence among universities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proficience would be advanced by more intelligence mutual between the universities of Europe, forming a fraternity or correspondence in learning across sovereignties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage inter-institutional communication, shared orders, and exchange of knowledge to leverage collective improvement rather than isolated and redundant efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey and publicly designate writers for neglected fields
rubrics_metrics.description: There has been little public designation of writers to pursue parts of knowledge not sufficiently laboured; a survey of learning should identify omissions and the state of disciplines to guide public designations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'perambulation of learning' — a recorded plot of what lies unmanured — will inform public selection and excite voluntary endeavours; designation and patronage should target genuine gaps rather than assuming plenitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compile a history of learning (literary history)
rubrics_metrics.description: A general state or history of learning from age to age (a history of learning) is lacking and should be composed to make learned men wise in the use and administration of learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond curiosity, such literary history reveals origins, sects, inventions, traditions, oppositions and causes of flourishing or decay; this institutional knowledge aids better policy and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect histories of Nature's irregulars and mechanical arts; separate superstition
rubrics_metrics.description: History of Nature should include (a) Nature in course, (b) Nature erring or varying (marvels), and (c) Nature altered or wrought (art); present collections of marvels and mechanical arts are weak and need substantial, severe collection with rejection of fables and sorting of superstition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically collect heteroclites and mechanical practices, examine and reject fables; where accounts mingle with superstition, sort them separately and investigate natural causes — some 'superstitious' reports may illuminate natural principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value mechanical/operative studies as foundational to natural philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: History mechanical (manual and operative arts) is the most radical and fundamental towards natural philosophy; mean and small things often disclose great truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disdain practical or mechanical inquiries; support manuals, experiments, and cross-transfer of observations among arts, since trials and vexations of art reveal variations of nature not seen in speculation alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer full texts, lives, and narrations; avoid epitomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Epitomes and abridgements have corroded many excellent histories; of histories, lives (biographies) and narrations of actions provide better verity and profit than mere chronicles or epitomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor complete works and carefully composed biographies/relations for accuracy and use; avoid relying on corrupt or truncated epitomes that erode original meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: National histories should be comprehensive and unified where fitting
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a deficiency in modern histories of the nation (example: England and Scotland); it would be honorable to produce a joined, continuous history of Great Britain to serve posterity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support comprehensive, well-composed national histories for instruction and memory; such works aid governance and collective memory and should be pursued with care rather than partial, biased accounts.
